ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, Canada's main railway trunk lines and city points are clearly concentrated in the southern region, especially along the Canada-U.S. border; they are distributed relatively densely near the Great Lakes-Saint Lawrence River basin and along the southwestern Pacific coast, while in Canada's vast northern region, railways and cities are both very sparse. Then reason: Southern Canada has a relatively lower latitude, relatively better heat conditions, a relatively large plain area, and at the same time convenient transportation and relatively good market conditions, making it suitable for the development of planting industry. Therefore, the agricultural regional distribution similar to the distribution pattern of railways and cities in the figure, "concentrated in the south and sparse in the north," is the planting industry area.
